goal: Replace visually rejected body-derived garment shells with an editable panel-and-seam workflow capable of producing customer-buyable VRChat outfits.

required: Publicly inspectable source code for ADOPT or PROTOTYPE decisions
Explicit software license before vendoring or commercial use
Separate review of code, model-weight, dataset, and asset licenses

implementationCandidates.name: GarmentCode
implementationCandidates.productionRole: Canonical editable representation for panels, edges, interfaces, seams, body measurements, and design parameters.
whyItSolvesCurrentFailure: Prevents a halter dress from being represented as disconnected body-surface bands.
Makes front, back, side, skirt, neckline, and halter straps explicit design components.
Allows silhouette edits at the pattern level instead of repeatedly distorting a finished mesh.
implementationCandidates.integrationBoundary: Add an adapter that converts product pattern specifications into GarmentCode/PyGarment data and imports the simulated result into the existing Blender checkpoint flow.
implementationCandidates.licenseCaveat: The MIT statement applies to repository code; datasets, body models, and third-party simulation dependencies require separate checks.

implementationCandidates.name: ZOZO's Contact Solver
implementationCandidates.productionRole: Offline draping, strain limiting, friction, self-contact, body contact, and penetration-resistant cloth simulation.

requirements.gpu: NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12.8 or newer support for the solver backend

whyItSolvesCurrentFailure: Produces cloth volume and folds from panels instead of inflating body-derived geometry.
Provides a stronger collision baseline for skirts, straps, lace overlays, and layered pieces.
Separates design geometry from the final draped state.
implementationCandidates.integrationBoundary: Run in an isolated Blender 5 simulation environment and import the baked mesh into the repository's pinned production Blender environment until the main toolchain is deliberately upgraded.
implementationCandidates.licenseCaveat: Preserve Apache-2.0 notices. Do not assume bundled examples or externally downloaded assets share the same license.

implementationCandidates.name: Material Maker
implementationCandidates.productionRole: Procedural fabric albedo, roughness, normal, height, opacity, and mask authoring independent of garment geometry.
whyItSolvesCurrentFailure: Replaces the current uniform plastic-like response with fabric-specific microstructure.
Supports separate satin, lace, elastic trim, and metal hardware material identities.
Makes material variants reproducible rather than hand-tuned per render.
implementationCandidates.integrationBoundary: Export deterministic PBR channel sets into Assets/GenWorks/<slug>/Textures and bind them through the existing material manifest.
implementationCandidates.licenseCaveat: Generated or imported third-party texture resources retain their own licenses.

implementationCandidates.name: ChatGarment
implementationCandidates.productionRole: Generate candidate GarmentCode patterns from an image or text description, then refine them through deterministic pattern validation.
whyItSolvesCurrentFailure: Can propose recognizable garment structure instead of producing an unstructured surface shell.
Its output can enter the GarmentCode representation selected as the canonical pattern layer.
Includes a postprocessing path for incorrect garment dimensions.
implementationCandidates.integrationBoundary: Use only as a proposal generator. Every output must pass panel validity, seam graph, dimensional, licensing, simulation, and human design review before becoming canonical.
implementationCandidates.licenseCaveat: Repository code is Apache-2.0, but model weights, training data, LLaVA/LISA dependencies, and any GPT-4o-assisted path require separate commercial and privacy review.

implementationCandidates.name: MakeClothes
implementationCandidates.productionRole: Reference implementation for fitting clothing assets to parameterized bodies and preserving reusable clothing metadata.
whyItIsNotPrimary: It targets the MakeHuman ecosystem rather than the Siroino avatar contract.
It does not replace the need for explicit pattern design or production cloth simulation.
implementationCandidates.integrationBoundary: Study transfer, body-zone, and fitting concepts; do not introduce a MakeHuman body dependency into Siroino products.

researchWatchlist.name: ReWeaver
researchWatchlist.reason: The publication says code and data will be available; a commercially reviewable licensed repository was not verified during this survey.

researchWatchlist.name: PatternGSL
researchWatchlist.reason: The paper announces a future code and data release. Do not depend on an unreleased or unlicensed implementation.

researchWatchlist.name: SwiftTailor
researchWatchlist.reason: The official project page lists code as TBD. Its geometry-image and dynamic-stitching ideas remain benchmark targets only.

researchWatchlist.name: AutoSew
researchWatchlist.reason: The paper states that code and data are available, but this survey did not verify a canonical repository URL and explicit license. Implement the seam-graph principle independently until those are verified.

researchWatchlist.name: NI-Tex
researchWatchlist.reason: Use uncertainty-guided multi-view PBR baking as a quality benchmark; no licensed implementation was verified for vendoring.

researchWatchlist.name: NaTex
researchWatchlist.reason: Use native 3D texture coherence and occlusion handling as a benchmark; no licensed source repository was verified for integration.

canonicalStages: simulation result cleanup while preserving panel identity
five-view, dynamic-pose, Unity, and customer-merchandising review
firstImplementationSlice: Create a GarmentCode halter mini-dress with explicit front bodice, back bodice, halter straps, fitted waist, front skirt, and back skirt panels.
Keep lace as a separate overlay panel or material mask rather than a solid inflated band.
Simulate the garment around the Siroino Large-profile body in ZOZO Contact Solver.
Author fabric-specific PBR channels in Material Maker.
Reject the candidate unless customers can identify the product as a halter dress from front, back, and three-quarter views without reading its name.
prohibitedShortcuts: Do not use body-surface vertex selection as the primary garment design representation.
Do not accept penetration-free geometry when the silhouette or garment construction is commercially unattractive.
Do not call a single dark glossy material lace, satin, and trim simultaneously.
Do not vendor code, models, datasets, or assets whose applicable license has not been verified.

productDecision.customerFinding: The current result reads as an inflated plastic body covering rather than a desirable lace halter dress.
productDecision.continuation: Preserve the checkpoint as rejection evidence, then rebuild from an explicit GarmentCode pattern and simulated cloth workflow instead of incrementally modifying the rejected mesh.
